 XVI ADDL.CITY CIVIL AND  SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT The plaintiff has filed this suit against the defendants praying to pass a judgment and decree of mandatory injunction and grant possession certificate in favour of the plaintiff in respect of Site No.303 and 304 of Sunkenahalli Adjacent Area Layout and further to declare that the endorsement dated 21.09.2011 issued by the first defendant and addressed to the plaintiff is illegal, not binding on the plaintiff and is liable to be quashed and to remove the construction put up on Site Nos.303 and 304 which are the suit schedule properties and further reliefs as are justice in the circumstances of the case.

2. Briefly stated, the case of the plaintiff is as under:-
Plaintiff's mother deceased Kamalabai had purchased two Revenue Sites bearing Nos.113 and 114 formed in Sy.No.51/1 of Gavipura Village, Bangalore under registered sale deed dated 13.09.1951 and thereafter, entire area wherein the sites purchased by deceased Kamalabhai is situated came to be acquired by the then CITB for formation of the Layout and thereafter, new numbers 303 and 304 were assigned to the sites of late Kamalabai.
As per the re- conveyance scheme of the first defendant, some of the site owners in the said area were issued with possession certificate corresponding to their old sites.
The mother of the plaintiff late Kamalabai also made representation to the BDA-first defendant for grant of possession certificate.

The plaintiff's mother was called upon by a letter dated 7.4.1983 to produce the Original Sale Deed and other relevant documents to the first defendant for issue of possession certificate, pursuant to which, late Kamalabai produced the original sale deed under which she purchased two sites, and other required documents to the first defendant on 15.07.1983 along with a covering letter.
The first defendant after receipt of the original sale deed from her, did not issue her the possession certificate.
Many representations were lodged with the first defendant claiming the possession certificate.
But her attempt was not fruitful.
One such representation dated 13.03.1984 is produced along with the plaint.
3. It is further averred by the plaintiff that his mother Kamalabai died on 21.08.1991 leaving behind her the plaintiff and her other children.

As per the directions of the BDA - the first defendant, the plaintiff got a release deed executed by the other legal heirs of deceased Kamalabai in his favour,
which is produced along with the plaint.

Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
2 4.

It is further averred that during the year 1982, the 2nd defendant filed a suit against the plaintiff and his deceased mother in OS No.943/1982 on the file of City Civil Court, Bangalore for permanent injunction alleging that the plaintiff herein and his mother are interfering with his possession of his site bearing No.1108 and in the said suit, the second defendant sought for an interim order and the said application came to be dismissed.

Aggrieved by the said order, 2nd defendant filed MFA 559/1982 before the High Court and during the pendency of the said appeal, 2 nd defendant filed an undertaking by way of Memo dated 15.06.1982 and sought for modification of the order and sought for permission and in the said Memo, he had undertaken to demolish the construction if it is found that he has constructed the building in the sites bearing No.303 and 304 belonging to the plaintiff.
Said Memo is produced along with the plaint and the said suit came to be dismissed on 2.1.1988.

Against the said judgment and decree in the said suit, the 2nd defendant preferred RFA No.224/1988 on the file of High Court and during the pendency of the said appeal, High Court by its order dated 22.7.1996, appointed an Engineer Commissioner to inspect and prepare a sketch identifying the properties of the plaintiff and the defendant No.2 with reference to Ex.P.9 which is the layout out plan of Hanumanthanagar issued by the Asst.Director, Town Planning Section BDA.
Accordingly, the Commissioner inspected the spot and prepared a sketch and the said sketch is produced.

After submission of the Commissioner's report, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by its order dated 4th September 1988 allowed the appeal and declared in the said appeal that, the plaintiff is the owner of sites bearing No.s 113 and 114 and the second defendant (The appellant in RFA 224/1988) is the owner of the Site No. 1108.
This could be seen from the decree passed in RFA 24/1988 which is produced along with the plaint.

After the decree in RFA 224/1988, the plaintiff made several representations to the first defendant to issue possession certificate an the representation dated 22-11-2007 and 26- 12-2007 made to the first defendant are produced along with the plaint.
The First Defendant issued an endorsement dated 16-07-2008 directing the plaintiff to produce the Release Deed of other heirs of deceased Kamalabai.
The plaintiff complied with the demand made by the First Defendant.
Acknowledgment for having submitted the Original Release Deed by deceased Kamalabi is produced along with the plaint.
5. The plaintiff submits that, he has been running pillar to pillar of the first defendant seeking them to issue possession certificate as he has been declared as the owner of site Nos.303 and 304.

The first defendant even though agreed on many occasions that the sites bearing Nos.303 sand 304 are corresponding revenue sites 113 and 114 of Gavipuram Village, has not issued possession certificate for the reason best known to them.
Further, the first defendant is postponing the issue of possession certificate and pleading that, they are unable to locate the sites and hence the delay in issuing possession certificate.

6. The plaintiff's further case is that the first defendant has been influenced by the second defendant in the matter and has been playing game upon the plaintiff who is the real owner of site Nos.303 and 304.

Even though the First Defendant has renumbered the revenue sites held by the plaintiff's mother as 303 and 304, has not issued Possession Certificate to the plaintiff inspite of many visit,
request, demand.

Hence this suit seeking direction of this Hon'ble Court to the First Defendant to locate, measure, identify and grant Possession of Certificate of site Nos. 303 and 304 in Gavipuram Adjacent area layout, and put him in possession of the same.
Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
3 7.

It is further averred that as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA 224/1988, it has already held that the plaintiff's mother is the owner of site bearing Nos.303 and 304 which are described in the suit schedule.

The plaintiff submits that after the decision was rendered, the plaintiff who was asked by the first defendant to comply with certain condition such as executing release deed by the other legal heirs of Kamalabai who is the mother of the plaintiff,
inspite of complying the demands made by the first defendant, as an afterthought, with a view to defraud the plaintiff, the first defendant did not chose to locate and handover possession certificate.
That after filing of the suit, the first defendant by an endorsement dated 21-09-2011 addressed to the plaintiff have stated that the plaintiff has sought for cancellation of site bearing No.1108 in favour of second defendant.
But, it is not so.
This plaintiff has not sought for cancellation of site bearing No. 1108 in favour of the second defendant.
On the other hand, the plaintiff has sought the first defendant to locate sites bearing Nos.303 and 304 and to issue possession certificate to the plaintiff.

The first defendant who has joined hands with the second defendant, has been misleading the plaintiff and also this Hon'ble Court has addressed an endorsement dated 21-09-2011 to the plaintiff wherein, they have stated that site Nos.1108, 303 and 304 are different sites and hence by virtue of decision in RFA 224/1988 they cannot interfere.

The endorsement dated 21-09-2011 issued by the first defendant is illegal, motivated and is issued by the first defendant in active connivance of second defendant which is not sustainable and the first defendant has done so in order to avoid their responsibility in locating and identifying the sites of the plaintiff.
Thus, the act of first endorsement dated 21-09-2011 is uncalled for, illegal and beyond scope of law,

The first defendant who has acquired the land belonging to the plaintiff and formed layout, renumbered the sites in accordance with the plan are bound under law to place the plaintiff in possession and issue possession certificate in respect of the site bearing Nos.303 and 304.
Without complying the mandatory responsibility the first defendant with ulterior motive in order to escape from their responsibility,

has issued the endorsement dated 21-09-2011 endorsing that they cannot interfere in the matter by virtue of the decision in RFA 224/1988 which is illegal and not sustainable and the endorsement issued by the first defendant is not lawful and is liable to be struck down as illegal.

8. The cause of action for the suit arose on and from the date of acquisition of the land belonging to the plaintiff's mother by the first defendant Vide Master Plan of BDA dated 15-11-1962 and on the date of representation dated 15-11- 1962 and on all date of repeated representations and on 7- 4-1983 being the date of call made by the First Defendant to produce the Original Sale Deed and other documents, and on 4-9-1998 being the date of Judgement and Decree in RFA 224/1988, and on 16-7-2008 when demand made by the First Defendant Release Deed and on subsequent dates of request and representations made by the plaintiff at Bangalore within the jurisdiction of this Court and the plaintiff has paid proper court fee on the plaint.
Hence, prayed to decree the suit.
9. The Defendant No-1 filed the written statement as hereunder:- The Defendant No.1 denies all the allegations made in the claim except those which are expressly admitted.
10. The suit of the plaintiff is false, frivolous, vexatious, misconceived and the same is not at all maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.

Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
4 11.
The plaintiff has not issued notice as contemplated under section 64 of the BDA Act.

Therefore,
the suit is bad in law and the plaint is liable to be rejected on that score only.

12. It is contended that the averments made in para 2 of the plaint that the plaintiffs mother deceased Kamalabai had purchased two revenue sites bearing Nos 113 & 114 formed in Sy No 51/1 Gavipura Village Bangalore, under registered sale deed dated 13/9/1951 is not within the knowledge of defendant No.1 and the plaintiff is put strict proof of the same.
It is further contended that the CITB has acquired the Sy. No.51/1 of Gavipura village for formation Layout called Sunkenahally adjacent sites layout.
It is further contended that the said village comes under Re- convey allotment scheme of the authority.
It is contended that the defendant No.1 issued possession certificate to site corresponding to their old sites.
It is contended that the plaintiff/s mother has also approached BDA for grant of certificate.

13. It is contended that the averments made in para 3 of the plaint that the plaintiff's mother Kamalabai died on 21/08/1991 leaving behind her the plaintiff and her other children and that the plaintiff got a release deed executed by the other legal heirs Kamalabai in his favour are not within the knowledge of the defendant and the plaintiff is to put strict proof of the same.

It is contended that the defendant No.1 is not party to the suit O.S.No.943/82, MFA No.559/82 and RFA No.
224/88.
14.

It is contended that the averments made in para 5 of the plaint that he has been running pillar to pillar of the first defendant seeking them to issue possession certificate as he has been declared as the owner of the site No 303 and 304, the first defendant even though agreed on many occasions that, the sites bearing Nos 303 and 304 are corresponding revenue sits 113 and 114 of Gavipuram Village are false and incorrect statement and the plaintiff is to put strict proof of the same.

It is further contended that in fact BDA has already issued an endorsement dated 21/09/2011 to the plaintiff informing him of its inability to interfere in the matter in view of the order passed by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in RFA 224/88.
The plaintiff has suppressed this fact before this court.

15. It is contended that the averments made in para 6 of the plaint that the first defendant has been influenced by the second defendant in the matter and has been playing the game upon the plaintiff who is the real owner of site Nos 303 and 304 and that even though the first defendant has renumbered the revenue sites held by the plaintiff's mother as 303 and 304 have not issued Possession Certificate to the plaintiff in spite of many visits, request, demand are all false and incorrect statement and the plaintiff is to put strict proof of the same.
It is contended that the defendant No.1 is not influenced by anybody much less the 2 nd defendant.

In the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA 224/88, it has observed that the plaintiff herein has failed to prove the encroachment by the 2nd defendant on the site belonging to the plaintiff.
In this view, the possession certificate is not issued.
The same is not deliberate.
16. It is contended that the suit is not maintainable since the plaintiff has not properly mentioned the schedule and boundaries of the suit property.

There is no cause of action for the suit and the alleged cause of action as stated in the plaint is false and the same is invented only for the purpose of Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/

17. In his written statement, the defendant No.2 has contended that the averments in Para 2 that the late mother of the Plaintiff purchased the revenue sites referred to therein and other relevant averments pertaining thereto are not within the knowledge of the 2 defendant and the Plaintiff is put to strict proof of the same.
18.

The averments in Para 3 of the Plaint as to the date of the death of the late mother of the Plaintiff, as to her legal heirs and as to execution of the Release Deed averred in Para 3 of the Plaint are the facts which are not in the knowledge of the defendant No.2 and the Plaintiff is put to strict proof of the same.

19. The averments in Para 4 of the plaint are all pertaining to proceedings O.S.No. 943 / 1982, MFA No. 559 / 1982, RFA No. 224/1998 and the averments in Para 4 also, the same are borne out by the records and as such they do not call for being traversed.
20.

In regard to the averments in Para 5, it is contended by the defendant No.2 that the plaintiff being not the owner of the sites referred to therein and as such the Plaintiff has not been able to obtain the possession certificate as to the said sites so far.
21.

With regard to the averments in Para 6, it is contended that they do not pertain to the 2nd Defendant and as such the question of traversing the same by Defendant 2 does not arise.
22.
As to the averments in Para 7 of the plaint, if the sum total of the plaint averments are cumulatively taken into consideration, the suit suffers from cause of action calling for summary dismissal.
23. It is contended that when the Plaintiff is not the owner schedule sites, the question of granting the relief of as sought by the Plaintiff in the suit does not arise.
24. In view of the above, the suit of the Plaintiff is frivolous, merit-less calling for summary dismissal and accordingly, the defendant No.2 prayed for dismissal of the suit with costs.

Additional Issues:
1: Whether the plaintiff proves his right and title over the suit schedule property?

6
2: Whether the plaintiff proves that the endorsement dated 21.09.2011 issued by the defendant No.1 is illegal and not binding on him?

3: Whether the plaintiff proves that defendant No.1 is under legal obligation to locate and identify the suit property and issue possession certificate in favour of the plaintiff as per the certificate in favour of the plaintiff as per the directions given him in RFA No.224/1998?
25.
In order to substantiate the contention of the plaintiff, the Plaintiff himself has got examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Exs.P.1 to P.19.
On the other hand, the defendant Nos.1 and 2 filed their written statements separately, but neither cross examined PW 1 nor came forward to lead any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
26. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for plaintiff, perused the materials placed on record.
On the other hand, despite sufficient opportunity, both the learned counsel for defendants did not address their argument.

27. The findings of this court on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 - In the affirmative, Addl. Issue No.1 - In the affirmative, Addl. Issue No.2 - In the affirmative, Addl. Issue No.3 - In the affirmative, Issue No.2 - As per final order, for the following - REASONS 28.
Additional Issue Nos.1 to 3 and Issue No 1 :-

These four issues are inter-connected to each other, therefore to avoid repeated discussions, they are taken up together here under:
29.
Admittedly, this suit is filed by the plaintiff on 03- 09-2010 against the defendants seeking the relief of mandatory injunction against defendant No.1

to locate, identify and grant possession certificate in favour of the plaintiff in respect of site Nos.303 and 304 in Sunkenahalli Adjacent Layout, as per sketch prepared by the Court Commissioner in RFA No.224/1988 as per Document No.7 in the suit; and to declare the endorsement dated 21-09-2011 issued by the 1st defendant and addressed to plaintiff as illegal not binding on the plaintiff and is liable to be quashed and prays for issue of direction to the 1 st defendant to locate,
identify and issue possession certificate in respect of sites bearing Nos.303 and 304 which are suit schedule properties and to comply with the direction as per order in RFA No 224/1988; and Direct the defendant to remove the construction done on Site Nos.303 and 304 which are the suit schedule properties by virtue of undertaking filed by him in MFA 559/1982 on the file of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka; and for other consequential reliefs as this Court deems fit.

7 30.

As per the above narrated case of the plaintiff, this suit has history way back from 1962 that is from the date of acquisition of the land belonging to the mother of the plaintiff by 1st defendant vide Master Plan of BDA dated 15-11-1962.
31.
To prove his case, the plaintiff himself entered into witness box and examined as PW1 and filed sworn affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief and in which all the plaint averments are reiterated.

To substantiate his case, he has produced certain documents which are marked as Exs.P 1 to Ex.P 19.
32.

According to plaintiff, his mother deceased Kamala Bai had purchased two revenue sites bearing No.113 and 114 formed in Sy.No.51/1 of Gavipura Village, Bangalore under registered sale deed dated 13-09-1951.

In this regard plaintiff has produced the certified copy of sale deed dated 13-09-1951 through which his mother Kamala Bai purchased Site Nos.113 and 114 from Sri Lingappa and Veerabhadrappa, who are the sons of Basappa for the sale consideration amount of Rs 500/-.
He has further stated that the original sale deed of the same is submitted to 1 st defendant BDA.

Ex.P.6 is the purchasers list with site numbers and address obtained on 06-06-1959 which shows site No.113 is purchased by Lingappa and Site No.114 is purchased by Veerabhadrappa, residents of No.69/3, 9 th Cross, II Main Road, Chamarajapet, Bangalore.

Their address corresponds with the address given in Ex.P.5.
33.
Ex.P.1 is the Letter dated 15-07-1983 given by Smt. Kamala Bai to 1st defendant BDA regarding allotment of sites No.303 and 304.

In the said document, it is mentioned by her that she has submitted the original sale deed dated 13-09-1951, the Encumbrance Certificate from 1-4-1970 to 23-04-1983 and re-conveyance from to BDA as per the direction of the Commissioner of BDA.
34.

Ex.P.3 is the Memo dated 15-06-1982 filed by the 2nd defendant B. S. Prithviraj in MFA No.559/1982 in which, he undertook that he will remove the construction put up on said site and will not claim any compensation thereof.
On the basis of said undertaking, he submitted to make the order of temporary injunction absolute.
In support of the same, the plaintiff has produced copy of order in MFA No. 559/1982 dated 15-06-1982.
The said MFA was filed by 2nd defendant herein against the Smt.Kamala Bai mother of plaintiff herein and R.Sathyanarayana, who is the plaintiff herein.

In page No.3 of the said document, it is observed by Hon'ble Justice that the defendants (
plaintiff herein and his mother) had brought suit O.S.No.3037/1981 in respect of site Nos.113 and 114 and obtained an injunction against one Bhaskar who is alleged to be holder of power of attorney of the plaintiff(2nd defendant herein) and it was contended that the plaintiff suppressing that fact had brought suit in the guise of constructing building on site No 1108 while actually he was constructing the building on site No.113 and 114.
This MFA filed by the 2 nd defendant herein against the order passed in IA No 1 in OS No.943/1982.
It is clear by above that in OS No.3037/1981 itself, the Hon'ble Court observed about the title of the mother of the plaintiff.
In page No.4, the recital of memo of the 2nd defendant that is Ex.P.3 is reflected.

35. Ex.P.7 is the encumbrance certificate in Form No.15 for the period of 1-4-1950 to 30-09-1966 which show the entry of sale deed dated 13-09-1951 executed by Lingappa and Veerabhadrappa in favour of Kamala Bai for sale consideration of Rs.500/- in respect of Site No.113 and 114 in Sy.No Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
8 51/1 of Gavipura village which corresponds with Exs.P.5.

is the encumbrance certificate in Form No.16 which shows no encumbrances in respect of site No.113 and 114 from 1-10-1966 to 31-03-1989.
36. Ex.P.16 is the certified copy of judgment and decree in OS No.943/1982 filed by 2nd defendant herein against the plaintiff and his mother for the relief of permanent injunction.
In that case, the suit schedule property is site No. 1108.

The said case was dismissed by giving finding that it is impossible to come to the conclusion whether the site in question is of the plaintiff or of the defendants, but ultimately the plaintiff has come into possession by giving an undertaking to the Hon'ble High Court.
Hence, until they decide their title in a proper suit, it is not possible for the plaintiff to succeed in that suit.
Against this judgment and decree defendant No.2 herein filed RFA No.224/1988 which is the main source for the present suit.

Ex.P.9 is the certified copy of interim order in RFA No.224/1988 under which Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka appointed an Engineer Commissioner and gave direction to 1st defendant here in to depute an Assistant Engineer working under his control to carry out the commission work.
37. Ex.P.10 is the judgment in RFA No.224/1988 dated 04-09-1998 in which the fact of renumbering of site Nos.113 and 114 as site Nos.303 and 304 is confirmed.

In page Nos.7 and 8 of Ex.P.10. the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka made a clear observation on the basis of commissioner report that the plots No.303 and 304 which are divided by 9th Main Road from the plaintiff's plot 1108.

Therefore, there can never be an impediment for declaring that the plot shown in the plan of the Asst.Executive Engineer, BDA dated 06-11-1997 is a plot of plaintiff and plot Nos.303 and 304 are the plots of the defendant and neither of them shall interfere with the possession of the other.

In the operative portion of the judgment, it was declared that the plaintiff is the owner of Plot No.1108 and the defendants are the owners of Plot Nos.303 and 304 and neither of them shall interfere with the possession and a decree for perpetual injunction shall follow as indicated above in favour of parties and plan shall form part of the decree.
38. Here, it is important to note that this order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka attained finality as it remained unchallenged.
Though both the defendants herein filed written statement, but nowhere they stated about challenge against this order.
It is very strange and even painful to note that the adjudication drawn in above RFA is on the basis of commissioner report made by the representative of BDA.
This order is passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka clearly declared the title of both the plaintiff and his mother herein and defendant No.2 herein in respect of their own sites ie. site No.303 and 304 in favour of plaintiff and his mother herein and Site No.1108 in favour of defendant No 2 herein.

Despite there being such a clear order from Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka which is one of the Apex Court to us to follow its directions, then the defendant No.1 here in from the year 1998 till 21-09-2011 as per Ex.P.19 by    merely stating that "    224-88     4-9-98    303, 304,  1108          
        
    ."
Surprising point is that the said commissioner report for proper adjudication in RFA No 224/1998 prepared by authorised person of 1st defendant only.

the defendant No.1 appeared through its counsel seeking to set aside exparte order and on 31-08-2012, it has filed its written statement after two years from the filing of the suit.

sentences.text: Ex.P.19 is the endorsement of BDA dated 21-09-2011.
It clearly shows the negligence from the side of defendant No.1 pertaining to this case.
This case is filed on 03-09-2010 as mentioned supra and this endorsement was issued to the plaintiff while this suit is pending.

On comparative discussion on the basis of dates, after this endorsement the defendant No.1 woke up from sleep and filed application to set aside ex-parte on 17-04-2012 after 6 months from issuance of endorsement.

After one adjournment from the order of setting aside exparte, filed its written statement which shows the "Tortoise Journey" of concerned authority established for public welfare by the government under the Constitution of India.
It is painful struggle of a common citizen to get his right though everything is administered under motto for the people, by the people and to the people.
39. In its written statement, it is stated that the sale deed of plaintiff is not within their knowledge and asked for strict proof of the same.
But Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka already declared the ownership of the plaintiff as supra then question of proving the ownership by prayer of declaration in this case does not arise at all.

In paragraph 7 of its written statement, it is stated that defendant No.1 agreed on many occasions that site Nos.303 and 304 are corresponding revenue sites Nos.113 and 114 of Gavipuram village are false and incorrect statement and asked the plaintiff to prove the same.
As per discussion supra, the identification of the said properties and renumbering of the said properties are done by this BDA itself.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka adjudicated the ownership of the plaintiff over site Nos.303 and 304 and defendant No.2 on site No. 1108 only on the basis of the commissioner report of BDA.

But now in this case, the same BDA is asking for the proof of the same which shows the attitude of defendant No.1 towards this case, towards their duty and towards the respect on the authenticity of the order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

When the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka itself cleared the ambiguity about ownership and possession of the parties over the suit schedule property, then what hindred/ is hindering defendant No.1 to grant possession certificate to the plaintiff?
is the big question before this court.

The location,
identification of the properties concluded by the defendant No.1 in RFA No 224/1988 through its own commissioner report and the said commissioner report plan is treated as part of the said judgment and decree by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, then why this defendant No.1 made delay and still not come forward to issue possession certificate to the plaintiff.

As per Ex.P.2, the mother of the plaintiff who was the 1st defendant in OS No 943/1982, 1st respondent in MFA No 559/1982, 1st respondent in RFA No 224/1988 and plaintiff in OS No 3037/1981 as per page No.3 of Ex.P 12 died on 21-08-1991.

This shows that after purchase of suit schedule property, till the date of her death, she has not enjoyed her right over the property in peaceful manner though her ownership was declared on 04-09-1998 till her death.
40. Though the defendant No.1 filed written statement but, did not cross examine PW 1 and did not take any pain to lead evidence to disprove the plaintiff's case and to defend it's side.

Though in page No.3, paragraph No 4 of the plaint, it is narrated about the memo of under taking about demolition of construction by defendant No.2, in paragraph 4 of his written statement, the defendant No 2 contended that "the averments in para 4 they all pertain to proceedings in O. S. No. 943/1982, MFA No.559/1982, RFA No.224/1998 and the averments in para 4 as to the same are borne out by the Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
10 records and as such they do not call for being traversed.

But as per materials on record, the suit schedule properties are same, and in those cases, this defendant was declared as owner of site No.1108 and he has undertaken that if he constructed building in site No.303 and 304 (old 113 and 114), he agreed to demolish the same by his own will and wish through said memo that is Ex.P 3.

Then definitely if there is construction in site Nos.303 and 304 by him if any, he is liable to demolish the same as he is not specifically denied about Ex.P 3.
41.
In Ex.P 11 sketch, it is specifically noted that sites Nos.305, 304 and 303 and road shown in Ex.D 9 between sites 303 and 110 is not existing at spot.

Ex.P.13 is the certified copy of memo dated 22-09-1971 issued by the government of Mysore shows the boundary of site No.499 as North Site No 450, South Site No.448, East by Road and West by Site No.305.

Ex.P.14 is the certified copy of re- conveyance/allotment of possession certificate in the name of Smt.Jayamma in respect of site No.451:1 which is bounded by in East Road, West Site No 1108, in the North Site No.452 and in the South Site No.450 and 451:2.

Ex.P.15 is the certified copy of re-conveyance/allotment of possession certificate in the name of Smt.Kamalamma in respect of site No 451:2 which is bounded by East by road, West by site No 451:1, North by site No 451:1 and South by site No 450.
While comparing these boundaries with Ex.P 11 sketch, the said properties are situated as per that boundaries only.
Then there is no doubt about the note mentioned in Ex.P 11 sketch and the defendant No 1 BDA itself properly identified the property through its own commissioner report.

42. Moreover, all these contents of Ex.P 11 sketch are accepted by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No 224/1988 and on the basis of the same, the ownership of the plaintiff and defendant No.2 is decided by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The same has attained finality as the judgment in RFA 224/1988 remained unchallenged and defendant No.2 has not denied the same in his written statement.

43. When the plaintiff has approached the BDA for possession certificate on the basis of order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, then this defendant No.1 has no ground to refuse to implement it as it is not the party to that RFA.

It is important to note that as supra the said judgment passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on the basis of report of commissioner and the sketch prepared by the commissioner which is marked as Ex.P 11.
The said court commissioner is none other than the Assistant Executive Engineer BDA as per signature and seal in Ex.P 11 sketch.

44. Though the said sketch issued by their department only, but as per Ex.P.17, the endorsement dated 22-11-2007 issued by the same BDA, they gave direction to this plaintiff to furnish the said sketch prepared by them in RFA No. 224/88.
As per Ex.P.18, the letter dated 26-11-2007 given by the plaintiff to defendant No.1 shows that the plaintiff has complied the direction given to him in Ex.P 17.
Though plaintiff done everything as directed by defendant No.1, but as per Ex.P.19, the defendant No.1 simply refused to interfere about possession as per order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Since the Hon'ble High Court has cleared the air, question of interfering in the order of the Hon'ble High Court does not arise.
In the said order Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka concluded on the question of ownership, identity and location of site No 303, 304 and 1108.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka gave clear picture on the sites where there is no impediment to issue possession certificate to the plaintiff in respect of site Nos.303 and 304.

As per Ex.P.17 and Ex.P 18, the Subject Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
11 in that document clearly shows that plaintiff filed representation to BDA in respect of Site Nos.303 and 304.
But in Ex.P.19 in its 'subject', it is mentioned as regarding allotment of site to the plaintiff herein after cancellation of site No.1108 in the name of 2nd defendant.

But in the judgment in RFA No 224/1988, it is clear that Site No.1108 is separate from Sites Nos.303 and 304 and specifically declared ownership of defendant No.2 over site No.1108 and ownership of plaintiff and his mother over site Nos.303 and 304, hence, there is no ambiguity about the sites and its ownership and there is no need of cancellation of site in the name of defendant No.2 pertaining to site No.1108 which shows that defendant No.1 is negligent in perusal of judgment in RFA No 24/1988 and failed to give proper attention to disposal of application of plaintiff for issuance of possession certificate in respect of Site Nos.303 and 304.

It is clear that plaintiff has not made representation before 1st defendant for cancellation of allotment of site No 1108 to defendant No 2 because the first prayer in this plaint clearly says that plaintiff prayed for issuance of possession certificate in favour of him in respect of site Nos.303 and 304 as per sketch prepared by the Court commissioner in RFA No 224/1988.
Though the defendant No.1 authority itself prepared the said sketch and produced it before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, now this defendant himself denying it, which is very strange of its kind.

45. Next to that, though the defendant Nos.1 in para 3 of his written statement, contended about non- issuance of notice under Section 64 of BDA Act prior to filing of the suit, but Exs.P.17 to 19 clearly shows that the plaintiff made several representation before defendant No.1 prior to filing of the suit and the same were replied by defendant No.1 as per Exs.P 17 to 19, that means defendant No.1 has notice of cause of action to this suit.

46. Morever, both the defendants after filing of their written statement have not come forward to cross examine PW 1 and did not take any pain to lead their evidence which leads to inference under Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act.
As per written statements also, there is no specific denial about the subject matter of the suit.
Therefore, there is no contra against plaintiffs pleading and evidence.
The documentary evidence of the plaintiff corroborate with oral evidence and pleadings of the plaintiff.

Moreover, as per above discussions and facts and circumstances of the case, the plaintiff has made out that he is owner of site Nos.303 and 304 of Sy No. 51/1 of Gavipura Village as per the order of Hon'ble High Court of Kanrnataka and there is no impediment to defendant No.1 to issue possession certificate to the plaintiff in respect of Site Nos.303 and 304.

The issuance of possession certificate pertaining to sites in said layout is made out as per Ex.P 13 and 14.
47.
If the defendant No.1 had complied the order of the High Court as above, then the precious time of the Court and energy of the parties could have been saved.

The lethargic and inattentive attitude on the part of the defendant No.1, it being a government institution, in disregarding clear and specific order of the Hon'ble High Court and in repudiation of its own documents, though calls for imposition of heavy cost on it, however by considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the above attitude of defendant No.1 in this case is strongly deprecated and reprimanded.
48. Thus, in view of the elaborate discussion made supra, it is clear that the plaintiff successfully proved his case to grant the relief as claimed in the plaint.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 and Addl.Issue Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the affirmative.

Sathyanarayana R vs Bda Commissioner on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65764217/
12 49.

Issue No.2:- For the discussions and reasons assigned in Issue No.1 and Addl.Issue Nos.1 to 3,
the suit of the plaintiff deserves to be decreed and hence, I pass the following:
ORDER The suit of the plaintiff is decreed in the following terms:-

It is hereby directed that the defendant No.1 shall locate, identify and grant possession certificate in favour of the plaintiff in respect of site Nos.303 and 304 in Sunkenahalli Adjacent Layout, Bengaluru, as per sketch prepared by the Court Commissioner in RFA No.224/1988;
It is hereby declared that the Endorsement dated 21-09-2011 issued by the 1 st defendant and addressed to plaintiff as illegal not binding on the plaintiff and the same is hereby quashed; and It is hereby directed that the defendants, especially defendant No.2, shall remove the construction put up on Site Nos.303 and 304 which are the suit schedule properties by virtue of undertaking filed by him in MFA 559/1982 on the file of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The defendants shall file a compliance report of the above order, within 2 months from the date of this order.
No order as to costs.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Aggrieved by the said order, 2nd defendant filed MFA 559/1982 before the High Court and during the pendency of the said appeal, 2 nd defendant filed an undertaking by way of Memo dated 15.06.1982 and sought for modification of the order and sought for permission and in the said Memo, he had undertaken to demolish the construction if it is found that he has constructed the building in the sites bearing No.303 and 304 belonging to the plaintiff.
Against the said judgment and decree in the said suit, the 2nd defendant preferred RFA No.224/1988 on the file of High Court and during the pendency of the said appeal, High Court by its order dated 22.7.1996, appointed an Engineer Commissioner to inspect and prepare a sketch identifying the properties of the plaintiff and the defendant No.2 with reference to Ex.P.9 which is the layout out plan of Hanumanthanagar issued by the Asst.Director, Town Planning Section BDA.
The First Defendant issued an endorsement dated 16-07-2008 directing the plaintiff to produce the Release Deed of other heirs of deceased Kamalabai.
The plaintiff complied with the demand made by the First Defendant.
8. The cause of action for the suit arose on and from the date of acquisition of the land belonging to the plaintiff's mother by the first defendant Vide Master Plan of BDA dated 15-11-1962 and on the date of representation dated 15-11- 1962 and on all date of repeated representations and on 7- 4-1983 being the date of call made by the First Defendant to produce the Original Sale Deed and other documents, and on 4-9-1998 being the date of Judgement and Decree in RFA 224/1988, and on 16-7-2008 when demand made by the First Defendant Release Deed and on subsequent dates of request and representations made by the plaintiff at Bangalore within the jurisdiction of this Court and the plaintiff has paid proper court fee on the plaint.
Hence, prayed to decree the suit.
9. The Defendant No-1 filed the written statement as hereunder:- The Defendant No.1 denies all the allegations made in the claim except those which are expressly admitted.
The plaintiff has not issued notice as contemplated under section 64 of the BDA Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The plaintiff submits that after the decision was rendered, the plaintiff who was asked by the first defendant to comply with certain condition such as executing release deed by the other legal heirs of Kamalabai who is the mother of the plaintiff,
inspite of complying the demands made by the first defendant, as an afterthought, with a view to defraud the plaintiff, the first defendant did not chose to locate and handover possession certificate.
That after filing of the suit, the first defendant by an endorsement dated 21-09-2011 addressed to the plaintiff have stated that the plaintiff has sought for cancellation of site bearing No.1108 in favour of second defendant.
The first defendant who has joined hands with the second defendant, has been misleading the plaintiff and also this Hon'ble Court has addressed an endorsement dated 21-09-2011 to the plaintiff wherein, they have stated that site Nos.1108, 303 and 304 are different sites and hence by virtue of decision in RFA 224/1988 they cannot interfere.
The endorsement dated 21-09-2011 issued by the first defendant is illegal, motivated and is issued by the first defendant in active connivance of second defendant which is not sustainable and the first defendant has done so in order to avoid their responsibility in locating and identifying the sites of the plaintiff.
Thus, the act of first endorsement dated 21-09-2011 is uncalled for, illegal and beyond scope of law,
The first defendant who has acquired the land belonging to the plaintiff and formed layout, renumbered the sites in accordance with the plan are bound under law to place the plaintiff in possession and issue possession certificate in respect of the site bearing Nos.303 and 304.
Without complying the mandatory responsibility the first defendant with ulterior motive in order to escape from their responsibility,
has issued the endorsement dated 21-09-2011 endorsing that they cannot interfere in the matter by virtue of the decision in RFA 224/1988 which is illegal and not sustainable and the endorsement issued by the first defendant is not lawful and is liable to be struck down as illegal.
Therefore,
the suit is bad in law and the plaint is liable to be rejected on that score only.
The averments in Para 3 of the Plaint as to the date of the death of the late mother of the Plaintiff, as to her legal heirs and as to execution of the Release Deed averred in Para 3 of the Plaint are the facts which are not in the knowledge of the defendant No.2 and the Plaintiff is put to strict proof of the same.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. The suit of the plaintiff is false, frivolous, vexatious, misconceived and the same is not at all maintainable either in law or on facts and the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
Therefore, there can never be an impediment for declaring that the plot shown in the plan of the Asst.Executive Engineer, BDA dated 06-11-1997 is a plot of plaintiff and plot Nos.303 and 304 are the plots of the defendant and neither of them shall interfere with the possession of the other.
In the operative portion of the judgment, it was declared that the plaintiff is the owner of Plot No.1108 and the defendants are the owners of Plot Nos.303 and 304 and neither of them shall interfere with the possession and a decree for perpetual injunction shall follow as indicated above in favour of parties and plan shall form part of the decree.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka clearly declared the title of both the plaintiff and his mother herein and defendant No.2 herein in respect of their own sites ie. site No.303 and 304 in favour of plaintiff and his mother herein and Site No.1108 in favour of defendant No 2 herein.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka adjudicated the ownership of the plaintiff over site Nos.303 and 304 and defendant No.2 on site No. 1108 only on the basis of the commissioner report of BDA.
The location,
identification of the properties concluded by the defendant No.1 in RFA No 224/1988 through its own commissioner report and the said commissioner report plan is treated as part of the said judgment and decree by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, then why this defendant No.1 made delay and still not come forward to issue possession certificate to the plaintiff.
This shows that after purchase of suit schedule property, till the date of her death, she has not enjoyed her right over the property in peaceful manner though her ownership was declared on 04-09-1998 till her death.
But in the judgment in RFA No 224/1988, it is clear that Site No.1108 is separate from Sites Nos.303 and 304 and specifically declared ownership of defendant No.2 over site No.1108 and ownership of plaintiff and his mother over site Nos.303 and 304, hence, there is no ambiguity about the sites and its ownership and there is no need of cancellation of site in the name of defendant No.2 pertaining to site No.1108 which shows that defendant No.1 is negligent in perusal of judgment in RFA No 24/1988 and failed to give proper attention to disposal of application of plaintiff for issuance of possession certificate in respect of Site Nos.303 and 304.
